raw.cause: The display was built with COCKPIT_FAULT=backdoor, so run_display() calls name_open("cockpit-gps") and then sends MSG_POSITION (0x1001, the '\x01\x10' payload) straight to gps on every tick, alongside its normal nav request. The calls all succeed and gps replies within a fraction of a millisecond. The problem is not a hang. It is a layering breach: display depends directly on gps, bypassing nav, which is the only process the contract allows to talk to gps.
raw.qnx_call: MsgSend in display (to gps via the coid from name_open("cockpit-gps"))
raw.fix_summary: Remove the direct gps connection from display. Display should get position only through nav's route reply, which already embeds the gps position. If display truly needs raw position, add a nav message type that forwards it. Do not add display -> gps to blueprint.yaml unless the architecture is deliberately changed.

finding: display talks to gps, which the contract does not allow
